Apple Watch

Smartwatch · 38mm, 40mm, 41mm, 42mm, 44mm, 45mm · 50m (Series 2 and later) · digital · 2023–2026

The Apple Watch is a line of smartwatches that integrate fitness tracking and health-oriented capabilities with the iOS ecosystem. Its signature design includes a rectangular case with rounded corners and a touch-sensitive display, controlled via a haptic-feedback Digital Crown and a side button.

The story

The first Apple Watch, unofficially known as Series 0, was released in April 2015, establishing Apple's presence in the wearables market. A significant update came in 2016 with the Series 2, which introduced water resistance up to 50 meters and built-in GPS. The Series 3, launched in 2017, was the first to offer cellular connectivity, allowing it to function more independently from an iPhone. A major redesign occurred with the Series 4 in 2018, featuring a larger display with thinner bezels and introducing an electrical heart sensor for ECG readings. Subsequent generations have continued to build on this foundation, with the Series 5 introducing an always-on display, the Series 6 adding a blood oxygen sensor, and later models further refining health sensors and processing power.
